readings.heading: Ὁ Ἀπόστολος — 1 Corinthians 15:29–38
verses: 29. Brothers and sisters: otherwise, what will people do who are baptised on behalf of the dead? If the dead are not raised at all, why are they baptised on behalf of the dead?
30. And why do we ourselves run risks every hour?
31. I die every day — I swear it by the pride I take in you, which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord.
32. If, merely on human terms, I fought wild beasts at Ephesus, what good did it do me, if the dead are not raised? "Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die."
33. Do not be led astray: "Bad company ruins good character."
34. Sober up, as you should, and stop sinning. Some of you have no knowledge of God — I say this to shame you.
35. But someone will ask: "How are the dead raised? And with what kind of body do they come?"
36. Fool — what you sow is not brought to life unless it dies.
37. And what you sow is not the body that is going to be; you sow a bare seed — of wheat, perhaps, or of some other plant.
38. But God gives it a body as he has willed, and to each of the seeds its own body.

readings.heading: Τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον — Matthew 21:23–27
verses: 23. At that time, when Jesus had come into the temple, the chief priests and the elders of the people came up to him while he was teaching and said: "By what authority are you doing these things? And who gave you this authority?"
24. Jesus answered them: "I will ask you one question too. If you answer me, I will tell you by what authority I do these things.
25. The baptism of John — where was it from? From heaven, or from men?" And they reasoned among themselves, saying: "If we say, 'From heaven,' he will say to us, 'Then why didn't you believe him?'
26. But if we say, 'From men,' we are afraid of the crowd — for everyone holds John to be a prophet."
27. And they answered Jesus and said: "We do not know." And he said to them: "Neither will I tell you by what authority I do these things."
